subject: Decision Making
title: Roman Augury and Bird Signs
description: A quick, practical guide to Roman Augury and Bird Signs.

hook.text: Roman generals watched birds before every battle. The direction of flight decided whether to attack or retreat.

buildup.text: Augurs were official priests trained to read bird patterns. No major decision happened without their approval.

discovery.text: The system gave leaders a way to delay unpopular choices. Bad omens meant waiting without losing face.

twist.text: One consul threw sacred chickens overboard when they gave bad omens. He lost the battle and 90 ships.

climax.text: Augury was a decision framework disguised as religion. It forced pauses and created social permission to wait.

punchline.text: Birds decided battles. Augury was really a pause button for leaders.

quiz.question: What practical purpose did Roman augury serve?
options: Giving leaders a face-saving way to delay decisions
